question: The access matrix approach to protection has the difficulty that

the matrix, if stored directly, is large and can be clumsy to manage
the matrix cannot be modified once it is created

it does not provide sufficient protection against external threats

the matrix, if not stored directly, can cause system failure
model_outputs: The access matrix approach to protection has the difficulty that the matrix, if stored directly, is large and can be clumsy to manage. This is because the matrix is a 2D array where each row represents a subject (e.g. a user or process) and each column represents an object (e.g. a file or resource). The cell at the intersection of a row and column represents the access rights of the subject to the object. This can result in a large and complex matrix, making it difficult to manage and update. The answer is (C).

model_outputs:
The subroutine GCD(I,J,K) calculates the greatest common divisor (GCD) of two positive integers I and J, and stores the result in K.

The subroutine uses the Euclidean algorithm to find the GCD. The algorithm repeatedly replaces I with J and J with the remainder of I divided by J, until J becomes 0. At that point, I is the GCD of the original I and J.

The output of the subroutine is the GCD of I and J, which is stored in K. The answer is (A).

question:
Let G = (V, E) be a finite directed acyclic graph with |E| > 0. Which of the following must be true?
I. G has a vertex with no incoming edge.
II. G has a vertex with no outgoing edge.
III. G has an isolated vertex, that is, one with neither an incoming edge nor an outgoing edge.
options: I and III only
None of the above
I and II only
II and III only
I, II, and a vertex with one outgoing edge
I, II, and a vertex with one incoming edge
All of the above (I, II, III)
II only
I only
III only
model_outputs:
A directed acyclic graph (DAG) is a graph with no cycles, so every edge has a direction and there are no edges that connect a vertex back to itself. A vertex with no incoming edge is called a source, and a vertex with no outgoing edge is called a sink.

Since G is a DAG, it must have at least one source (a vertex with no incoming edge) and at least one sink (a vertex with no outgoing edge). Therefore, options I and II must be true.

Option III is also true because a vertex with neither an incoming edge nor an outgoing edge is an isolated vertex, which is a valid vertex in a DAG.

The answer is (G).
